procedure: Wind the wire over the iron nail to form a coil.
Suspend the coil by means of thread tied to its centre.
Connect the ends of the wire to the battery through the switch.
Keeping the switch OFF, bring some paper clips near to one end of the nail and observe whether they stick to the nail.
Turn the switch ON and again bring the paper clips near to the end of the nail. Observe whether they stick.
Turn the switch OFF and observe what happens to the clips.
aim: To show that an iron nail becomes a temporary magnet when electric current passes through a coil wound around it.

viva.question: What is an electromagnet?
viva.answer: A magnet produced when electric current passes through a coil of wire around an iron object.

viva.question: What happens to the iron nail when the switch is turned ON?
viva.answer: It becomes magnetized and can attract paper clips.

viva.question: What happens to the nail’s magnetism when the switch is turned OFF?
viva.answer: The nail no longer remains a magnet, so the clips fall.

viva.question: What is the role of the iron nail?
viva.answer: It acts as the iron core that becomes magnetized by the coil’s magnetic field.

viva.question: How can the strength of the electromagnet be increased?
viva.answer: By increasing the number of cells or the number of turns in the coil.

diagram: Draw a coil wound around an iron nail, suspended by a thread and connected through a switch to a battery, with paper clips near one end of the nail; label Thread, Coil, Iron Nail, Clips, Switch and Battery.
title: Making an electromagnet
precautions: Keep the switch OFF while setting up the circuit.
Ensure the wire is wound securely around the nail.
Make firm connections between the wire, switch and battery.
Turn the switch OFF when observations are complete to avoid unnecessary heating of the wire.
result: The iron nail attracts paper clips when current passes through the coil, showing that it becomes a temporary magnet. When the current is stopped, it no longer remains a magnet.
